## TL;DR

Task branches kept accumulating *other* tasks' board bookkeeping (`work/<other-id>-*.md`
and `work/reports/<other-id>/**`), so `repoos landable` refused to land them with
"the diff changes another task's bookkeeping", reviewers asked for the files to be
restored, the engineer restored them, and the next self-check re-committed them — a loop
that burned review rounds on #1058, #1060 and #1061. I reproduced the mechanism, fixed
the three code paths that could let a sibling's file onto a branch, added a handoff-time
repair, and covered it with tests.

## Work and rationale

**Root cause (reproduced).** The engineer self-check's WIP checkpoint,
`commitWipCheckpointForRemoteGate` in `src/server/engineer-remote-self-check.ts`, staged
only the task's own work with `git add -- <path>` but then ran a bare `git commit`. A
bare commit commits the *entire index*, not just the paths passed to `git add`. The
server continuously rewrites `work/*.md` on main; when a board write or a merge left a
sibling's file dirty and staged in the worktree, the WIP commit swept it onto the
branch. I confirmed this with a scratch fixture: a foreign `work/9999-other.md` and its
report, staged, were folded into a `WIP: engineer self-check checkpoint` commit. Once on
the branch, `git diff main...HEAD` reported drift, the landing preflight failed, and the
loop repeated because the next self-check re-ran the same sweep.

**Fix 1 — the checkpoint commits only what it intends (acceptance criterion 2).** Two
changes in `commitWipCheckpointForRemoteGate`: it now resets any foreign `work/`
bookkeeping out of the index before committing, and it commits with the pathspec form
`git commit -m <msg> -- <paths>`. The pathspec form is the real guard: even if something
slips into the index between staging and the commit, only the named paths can land. The
new core helper `foreignTaskBookkeepingPaths` (`src/core/git.ts`) classifies a path as a
sibling's bookkeeping when it is a `work/<other-id>-*.md` task file or lives under
`work/reports/` / `work/engineering-reports/` and is not this task's own report. I had to
teach it about reports explicitly: `isTaskBookkeepingPath` only returns true for the
task's *own* reports, so reusing it verbatim silently missed foreign reports.

**Fix 2 — handoff repairs a branch that already drifted (criterion 3).** Drift already
committed by an earlier WIP checkpoint is not fixed by guarding new commits, so handoff
now heals it. `restoreForeignTaskBookkeepingFromMain` (core, `git.ts`) runs in
`runHandoffFinalization` right after `guardReviewTransition` and *before* the check
snapshot and the review lock. It diffs the branch against its merge-base, finds foreign
bookkeeping, restores main's copy for modified/deleted files, `git rm`s branch-added
siblings, and lands the whole thing as one plain bookkeeping commit. That ordering
matters: running before the `worktreeState` snapshot means the cleanup commit is not
misread as "the worktree changed while the gate was running", and running before the
review lock means the lock records the healed HEAD. The restore is reported through
`opts.onTaskLog` rather than failing the handoff. I also extended the report-at-head
recognition so a retry after a restore still finds the finalized report.

**Fix 3 — documentation of the write paths (criterion 1).** I inventoried where siblings
reach a worktree: the server does *not* deliberately write a sibling's file into a
worktree (activity, CTO notes and watchdog writes go to `config.root`/main). They arrive
indirectly — via the WIP checkpoint's bare commit, a `git add -A` sweep, or a merge of
main. This is now written down in `docs/agent-workflow-rules.md`, and
`docs/close-out-pipeline.md`'s "Foreign bookkeeping drift" section lists the new guards.
AGENTS.md carries a one-line rule plus a link, staying under the 30 KB cap.

**Criterion 4 (naming the files and cause).** The landing preflight's "Task scope" check
already names the offending files and the cause in plain English; I verified it in a test
against a real branch. The handoff report now names the restored files in the task log.

## Approaches tried

I first assumed the WIP checkpoint's `uncommittedWorkFiles(..., workFileFilter)` was the
leak, since it excludes the whole `work/` tree. It does — so the dirty-file list never
contains work files; the leak was the already-staged index being committed wholesale. I
considered scoping via `git commit --only` vs `git reset` + pathspec; the pathspec form
`git commit -- <paths>` is simpler and cannot be defeated by a concurrent staging write,
so I used it and added the reset as belt-and-braces. For the handoff repair I initially
considered reusing `resetForeignWorkFiles` from `integration-orchestrator.ts`, but it
diffs against a passed-in main sha and lives in the server layer; a core function that
resolves the merge-base itself keeps the handoff path self-contained and testable.

## Challenges and blockers

The subtlest part was the reports classification: `isTaskBookkeepingPath` is asymmetric
(it treats only the caller's own reports as bookkeeping), so a naive reuse would have left
foreign reports on the branch. The second was ordering in handoff — the repair had to run
outside the gate's `before`/`after` drift window and before the review lock. No blockers;
no human step is required for this task.

## Key learnings

A bare `git commit` in an agent worktree is never safe when anything else can stage into
that index. Scoped `git add` does not scope `git commit`. And "keep main authoritative for
foreign task files" belongs at every commit boundary a task branch can cross — the WIP
checkpoint, the handoff commit gate, and close-out — not just at close-out.
